Extract dominant height from a CHM for a set of spatial units

Source: R/utils-chm.R
extract_h_dom.Rd

For each polygon unit, computes the dominant height \(H_{dom}\) as a high percentile (default 90%) of the canopy-height pixels falling inside that unit. Pixels with NA (typically masked by sanitize_chm) are ignored.

Usage

extract_h_dom(chm, units, percentile = 0.9, min_pixels = 10L)

Arguments

chm

A SpatRaster of canopy heights in metres. Typically the chm_clean component returned by sanitize_chm.

units

An sf polygon layer. One row per spatial unit.

percentile

Numeric in [0, 1]. The percentile of canopy heights to take as dominant height. Default 0.9.

min_pixels

Integer. Minimum number of non-NA pixels required to compute \(H_{dom}\). Units with fewer pixels get NA. Default 10.

Value

A numeric vector of length nrow(units) containing the dominant height (in metres) for each unit. NA when the unit holds fewer than min_pixels valid pixels.

Details

The convention \(H_{dom} = P_{90}(\mathrm{CHM})\) is a practical proxy for the classical definition (mean height of the 100 largest trees per hectare) when only a CHM raster is available. Choosing percentile = 1 yields the maximum height, percentile = 0.5 the median.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
chm_clean <- sanitize_chm(chm, forest_mask = bd_foret)$chm_clean
units$H_dom <- extract_h_dom(chm_clean, units)
} # }
